'''Stephen Robert Leone''' (born May 19, 1948) is an American physical chemist and the John R. Thomas Endowed Chair in Physical Chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="bphys"/><ref name="bchem">{{cite news |title=Stephen R. Leone |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/leone |accessdate=December 19, 2018 |publisher=University of California, Berkeley}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Leone was born in [[Queens]], [[New York City]], on May 19, 1948, of Italian descent. The family moved to [[Rochester, New Hampshire]], and later [[Batavia, Illinois]], where Stephen attended primary and secondary school. Leone earned a bachelor's degree from [[Northwestern University]] and spent a summer working at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] prior to attending the [[University of California, Berkeley]] for graduate study. In 1974, Leone began teaching at the [[University of Southern California]], and later moved to [[JILA]], a research institute at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]]. Leone returned to Berkeley in 2002.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Leone |first1=Stephen R. |title=Autobiography of Stephen R. Leone |journal=J. Phys. Chem. A |date=September 25, 2008 |volume=112 |issue=39 |pages=9169–9176 |doi=10.1021/jp8062564|pmid=18817359 |bibcode=2008JPCA..112.9169L }}</ref> He was [[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[Annual Review of Physical Chemistry]]'' from 2002&ndash;2011, retiring as editor in 2011;<ref name="AR2012">{{Cite journal|last1=Johnson|first1=Mark A.|last2=Martinez|first2=Todd J.|date=April 4, 2012|title=Preface|journal=Annual Review of Physical Chemistry|volume=63|issue=1|doi=10.1146/annurev-pc-63-040412-100001|issn=0066-426X|doi-access=free}}</ref> and is credited for organizing the volumes for 2012&ndash;2013.<ref name="AR2013">{{cite web |title=Editor of the Annual Review of Physical Chemistry - Volume 64, 2013 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?2013,physchem |website=Annual Reviews |access-date=August 2, 2021}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Over the course of his career, Leone has received the [[ACS Award in Pure Chemistry]] (1982) and [[Peter Debye Award]] (2005) from the [[American Chemical Society]], the [[Bourke Award]] (1995) and [[Polanyi Medal]] (2010) from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and the [[Herbert P. Broida Prize]] (1989) of the [[American Physical Society]], among several others.<ref name="bchem"/><ref name="bphys">{{cite news |title=Stephen Leone |url=http://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/Stephen-Leone |accessdate=December 19, 2018 |publisher=University of California, Berkeley}}</ref> He has been awarded Sloan and Guggenheim fellowships,<ref name="bchem"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Stephen R. Leone |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/stephen-r-leone/ |accessdate=December 19, 2018 |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation}}</ref> and was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 1995.<ref>{{cite news |title=Stephen R. Leone |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/stephen-r-leone-dtkeoz/ |access-date=December 19, 2018 |publisher=United States National Academy of Sciences}}</ref>
